skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised pet video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses account identities, stores tokens locally, and can query historical cloud reports with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: The skill sends media or URLs to configured backend APIs and the default configuration can use development/private HTTP endpoints, which is high-impact for potentially sensitive video content.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No destructive install hook, background service, or persistence daemon was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though runtime behavior writes a shared workspace database.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest directs automatic history lookup and says identity values must not be shown or requested from the user, reducing clear opt-in and user control for sensitive account-linked actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Runtime code reads a workspace key file, creates or reuses a default open-id, silently registers/logs in with a health-service endpoint, and persists user records plus access/open tokens in SQLite.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Local-file and URL-based heat-stress analysis is coherent with the stated purpose, but historical report listing and automatic account/session handling expand the capability into cloud account and report management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Only use it if you are comfortable sending pet videos or video URLs to the configured backend service, allowing automatic account linkage/registration, storing service tokens in a workspace SQLite database, and permitting cloud history report lookup. Prefer an isolated workspace and require explicit confirmation before history queries or media upload.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell invocation, local file reads, and network API calls fit a cloud-backed media analysis skill, but formal/user-facing disclosure is incomplete for identity and token behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic identity creation/reuse, token persistence, and cloud history retrieval are materially broader than simple current-video analysis even though the manifest partially documents them.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The --list report history path is present and can enumerate prior cloud reports; the generic ai_chat path is dormant/commented and was downgraded as non-material by itself.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad trigger phrases can automatically query historical cloud reports, which is sensitive enough to require clearer user confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill forwards local media or URLs to a backend and automatically attaches account identity data; consent and retention boundaries are not clearly presented to the user.
[E1] unexpected: External transmission for analysis is expected, but silent registration/login to the health service with derived identity fields is the concerning part.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filters are in an internal DAO helper and are not direct code execution; this was downgraded relative to the identity and history concerns.
[P2] expected: The flagged hidden-character evidence appears tied to ordinary emoji formatting, and no concealed directive was found in the manifest.
[YR4] expected: The metadata is long and bilingual but does not show concrete tool-poisoning instructions; this did not drive the verdict.
